scope: Expected results for the existing page-type/language word-count policy. Authored before implementation; not labels of general semantic content quality.

cases.judge_reason: A contact page has its own existing 80-word benchmark; imposing 300 changes the producer rule.
A landing page exceeds its existing benchmark, even though it is below 300.
The producer measures a 150-word deficit against its news benchmark. The global 300 rule misses that result.
The existing FAQ benchmark is 400; this is contract consistency, not a claim that all 350-word FAQs lack value.
The producer's other-page benchmark is met; the aggregator must not replace it with 300.
Wire the already-defined French multiplier to the detected language; do not invent a new coefficient.
The existing Arabic contact policy is 64 words; preserve the language and benchmark as evidence.
The established French product rule passes this count; a fixed 300-word consumer contradicts it.
The existing comparison is strictly below the benchmark; equality is not a deficit.
